## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
*Āvudhapāṇi* ("Holding a weapon") is the sixtieth training rule (*sekhiya*) in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Like other rules in this section of the code of conduct, it regulates monastic deportment, specifically addressing conduct regarding teaching the Dhamma to a person who is holding a weapon [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this training rule is shared across Buddhist monastic traditions [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali canon, it corresponds directly to the sixtieth rule in the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha*, the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga*, and the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha*, as well as the corresponding sections of the *Parivāra* [SuttaCentral]. Beyond the Theravāda tradition, parallels are preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan texts from the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, and Lokottaravāda Vinayas [SuttaCentral].
In automated text-reuse analyses conducted by DharmaNexus, the text exhibits 79 matching passages with 29 other Pali texts, particularly sharing long introductory and formulaic segments with adjacent rules in the *Sekhiya* chapter (notably Sk 58, Sk 59, and Sk 61–72) [DharmaNexus]. Modern English translations of the rule include that by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
